newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot to seek code-sharing with Latvian airline.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot to seek code-sharing with Latvian airline.

text.p: Russia's Aeroflot International Airlines plans to sign a code-sharing agreement with Latvian private airline Air Baltic Corporation (ABC), an Aeroflot official said on Wednesday.
The move was aimed at defusing a row over flights between Moscow and the Latvian capital Riga.

Leonid Mokhov, deputy chief of Aeroflot CIS and Baltic states department, told Reuters that Latvian aviation authorities had warned Aeroflot on Tuesday that its flights would be delayed because Russia and Latvia did not have a governmental agreement on regular air services.
But Mokhov said the new agreement should resolve the dispute by ensuring a balance on the market for regular services between Russia and Latvia.
Currently, Russia's Aeroflot and Transaero and Latvian airline RiAir fly between Moscow and Riga.
"Transaero and RiAir have a code-sharing agreement. We want to have the same agreement with ABC to make balance," Mokhov said, adding that ABC did not enough planes to operate the Riga-Moscow route.
Aeroflot flies between Moscow and Riga four times a week operating Tupolev-134 jets.
